name: aeon_party
description: The party transitions around an aeon: the summon, the arrival step, the dismissal, the aeon wipe, the lists swap and the Switch swap (FUN_007adf90, 7ade10, 7adae0, 7aef20, 7aeec0, 7adf10, 78e0a0).

harness.note: the real machine code of the functions; only the battle RNG function is replaced by a script (rngDraws is what the game asked for)

notes: in.world: active, saved (7 character ids, 255 = nobody), roster, rosterSaved (17 ids), g {summon, aeon, summoner, grand, actor, deadMask} (VA 0x0112c9e7, 9e8, 9e9, 0x0112ca03, 0x0112c9e4, 0x0112c90c), reward (18 bytes at VA 0x02310ea0), chr {id: the bytes of that character in this order: present, dc8, dc9, df8, dcb, f1a, summoner, arrival, blocked, dead, hp, ctb, perm, provoker, thrA, thrB, gauge, gaugeMax, gaugeSaved, gaugeHeld, stoned, baseCtb, recover, recoverMax, avail}. A character that is not listed is the default row: summoner, provoker, thrA and thrB 255, everything else 0.
in.ops: summon [summoner, aeon], arrive, drain (the queued arrival action finishes; nothing to do), dismiss [reviveFallen], restore, wipe, swap [out, in, mode].

out.steps: one entry per op, holding only what changed since the step before (the input world for the first op): the lists and reward arrays that changed, g {changed globals}, chr {id: {field name: new value} for every character field that changed}.

Every stored answer is the machine's own: the real code of FFX.exe, with only the battle RNG and the presentation functions that never touch the stored fields replaced (see research/re-ffx-overdrive-steal-aeons.md section 4.9).
